verification.spec: Verify there is a script/entrypoint that, given (hardware, kernel), iterates over every input shape in the testing dataset, enumerates all valid configurations in C_macro x C_micro for that kernel, benchmarks each with the standard warmup/measure protocol, and writes an oracle artifact mapping input_shape -> (best_config, best_latency). Run it on a small sub-sample (e.g., 5 shapes) and confirm output contains one best config per input shape and best_latency equals the min over the enumerated candidates.

sub_tasks.requirements: The exhaustive brute-force oracle collection takes on the order of 10 to 600 GPU hours per ⟨hardware, kernel⟩ pair, depending on workload scale, kernel complexity, and hardware characteristics.

verification.spec: Run the exhaustive brute-force oracle script on one full (hardware, kernel) testing dataset pair (e.g., Dense GEMM on H100) and record wall-clock GPU-hours. Confirm the elapsed time lies in the reported range of ~10-600 GPU hours (order-of-magnitude claim). Alternatively, project via a 1% sub-sample and extrapolate; assert projected total falls in [10, 600].

sub_tasks.requirements: Micro-config enumeration and dataset schema.
For each structural anchor ⟨G, L, c_macro⟩ in the training dataset, code enumerates and evaluates all feasible micro configurations c_micro ∈ C_micro (subject to hardware resource constraints).

verification.spec: For a fixed (G, L, c_macro) anchor of any kernel, invoke the profiling routine and record the set of c_micro evaluated. Assert this set equals the enumeration of feasible C_micro (given hardware resource constraints such as shared-memory/register budgets). Cross-check that infeasible c_micro (e.g., pipeline stages exceeding shared memory) are properly excluded rather than silently failing.

sub_tasks.requirements: The training profiling sample count follows N_profile = |C_macro| · W · I · |L| · |C_micro|, respecting the wave-aware sparse sampling budget rather than a dense sweep.

verification.spec: Enumerate all planned profiling samples for a small synthetic setup (e.g., |C_macro|=2, W=3, I=2, |L|=2, |C_micro|=4) and assert the total planned sample count equals |C_macro| * W * I * |L| * |C_micro|. Also verify actual number of executed profile trials matches this product (accounting for feasibility filtering).

sub_tasks.requirements: The unified Φ: X → (G, L) mapping and the decomposition of the configuration space C into macro and micro subspaces are implemented correctly for Dense GEMM, Grouped GEMM (MoE), and FlashAttention as specified in Table 2.

The unified logical-to-physical input mapping Φ: X → (G, L) is implemented as a shared abstraction that reduces heterogeneous kernel-specific input shapes into the 2D physical coordinate system (Grid Size G, Loop Count L).

Code has been implemented that defines a common interface/function Φ mapping arbitrary kernel logical inputs x ∈ X to the tuple (G, L), dispatching to per-kernel implementations for Dense GEMM, Grouped GEMM, and FlashAttention.

verification.spec: Call the unified mapping Φ(x, kernel_type, cmacro) with representative inputs for each kernel: (1) Dense GEMM with M=4096,N=4096,K=4096 and T_M=T_N=128,T_K=64 returns G=1024, L=64; (2) Grouped GEMM with total tokens summed across experts computes G as sum of ceil(M_i/T_M)*ceil(N/T_N); (3) FlashAttention with N_h=32, S_q=2048, S_kv=2048 and T_Q=128,T_KV=64 returns G=32*ceil(2048/128)=512, L=ceil(2048/64)=32. All three must dispatch through a single Φ interface.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, given (G, L) together with a macro-config, computes the wave count w = ⌈G / N_SM⌉ using the target GPU's SM count.

verification.spec: Import the wave-count function; call it with several (G, macro_config, device_sm_count) triples, e.g., (G=100, N_SM=132) -> 1, (G=132, N_SM=132) -> 1, (G=133, N_SM=132) -> 2, (G=264, N_SM=132) -> 2, (G=265, N_SM=132) -> 3. Assert output equals math.ceil(G / N_SM) in all cases. Also verify N_SM is derived from torch.cuda.get_device_properties (or equivalent) rather than hardcoded.

sub_tasks.requirements: Input mapping and configuration decomposition for Dense GEMM follow Table 2, with logical inputs (M, N, K), macro-config (T_M, T_N, T_K), micro-config (N_stg, N_wrp, ...), G = ⌈M/T_M⌉·⌈N/T_N⌉, and L = ⌈K/T_K⌉.
Code has been implemented that computes Dense GEMM grid size G = ⌈M/T_M⌉ · ⌈N/T_N⌉ from logical inputs (M, N, K) and macro-config (T_M, T_N, T_K).

verification.spec: Import the Dense GEMM grid-size function. For test cases such as (M=1024, N=1024, K=4096, T_M=128, T_N=64, T_K=64) -> ceil(1024/128)*ceil(1024/64) = 8*16 = 128; (M=1000, N=500, T_M=128, T_N=64) -> ceil(1000/128)*ceil(500/64) = 8*8 = 64; (M=64, N=384, T_M=128, T_N=64) -> 1*6 = 6. Assert exact equality.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes Dense GEMM loop count L = ⌈K/T_K⌉ from K and macro-config T_K.

verification.spec: Import the Dense GEMM input-mapping function Φ and call it with several (M, N, K) and c_macro=(T_M, T_N, T_K) values. Assert returned L equals ceil(K / T_K) for each case, including edge cases where K is not divisible by T_K.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Dense GEMM configuration space is decomposed such that C_macro consists of tile sizes (T_M, T_N, T_K) and C_micro consists of implementation-level parameters (pipeline stages N_stg, number of warps N_wrp, and other DeepGEMM tunables such as swizzling/rasterization).

verification.spec: Inspect the Dense GEMM configuration enumeration module. Assert C_macro is defined over (T_M, T_N, T_K) tile dimensions and C_micro is defined over pipeline stages, warp count, and additional DeepGEMM tunables (e.g., swizzling/rasterization). Confirm the split matches the shared schema c=(c_macro, c_micro).

sub_tasks.requirements: Dense GEMM's enumerated (C_macro × C_micro) valid configuration space matches the DeepGEMM candidate set (on the order of ~3,000 candidates spanning >10 tunable parameters) reported in the paper.

verification.spec: Enumerate |C_macro x C_micro| for the DeepGEMM Dense GEMM kernel using the implementation's enumeration API and assert the total count is on the order of 3000 (roughly 1500-6000) and that at least 10 distinct tunable parameter dimensions are present in the config schema.

sub_tasks.requirements: Input mapping and configuration decomposition for Grouped GEMM (MoE) follow Table 2, with logical inputs (M_i, N, K, E), macro-config (T_M, T_N, T_K), micro-config (N_stg, N_wrp, ...), G = Σ_{i=1..E} ⌈M_i/T_M⌉·⌈N/T_N⌉, and L = ⌈K/T_K⌉.
Code has been implemented that computes Grouped GEMM grid size G as the sum over experts G = Σ_{i=1..E} ⌈M_i/T_M⌉ · ⌈N/T_N⌉, where M_i is the number of tokens routed to expert i.

verification.spec: Import the Grouped GEMM grid-size function. Provide test inputs like E=4 experts with M_i=[100, 200, 50, 400], N=1024, T_M=128, T_N=64. Expected G = sum_i ceil(M_i/128) * ceil(1024/64) = (1+2+1+4)*16 = 128. Assert exact equality across several such cases including edge cases where some M_i=0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes Grouped GEMM loop count L = ⌈K/T_K⌉ from K and macro-config T_K.

verification.spec: Import the Grouped GEMM input-mapping function and call with several (M_i, N, K, E) inputs and c_macro=(T_M, T_N, T_K). Assert returned L equals ceil(K / T_K), independent of E and per-expert token counts.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, for runtime Grouped GEMM Φ evaluation, applies a uniform-across-experts approximation of per-expert token counts M_i (to avoid CPU-GPU synchronization on the dynamic routing distribution) as described in Section 5.2.

verification.spec: Invoke the runtime Grouped GEMM Phi mapping with total tokens T=1024 and E=8 experts (routing distribution NOT provided). Confirm code does not attempt any GPU->CPU sync on router outputs and instead uses uniform approximation M_i ≈ T/E = 128 for all i, yielding G = E * ceil(128/T_M) * ceil(N/T_N). Repeat with E=32, T=4096. Assert the returned G matches the uniform-approximation formula, not a per-expert distribution.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Grouped GEMM configuration space is decomposed into C_macro = (T_M, T_N, T_K) and C_micro = (N_stg, N_wrp, ...) matching the SGLang Triton MoE kernel's tunable parameter set.

verification.spec: Inspect the Grouped GEMM config enumeration. Assert C_macro=(T_M, T_N, T_K) and C_micro includes N_stg, N_wrp and other SGLang Triton MoE tunables. Cross-reference the parameter names/ranges against the upstream SGLang Triton MoE kernel's autotune configuration set.

sub_tasks.requirements: Input mapping and configuration decomposition for FlashAttention follow Table 2, with logical inputs (N_h, S_q, S_kv), macro-config (T_Q, T_KV), micro-config (N_stg, N_wrp, ...), G = N_h · ⌈S_q/T_Q⌉, and L = ⌈S_kv/T_KV⌉.
Code has been implemented that computes FlashAttention grid size G = N_h · ⌈S_q / T_Q⌉ from the number of query heads and query sequence length under macro-config T_Q.

verification.spec: Import the FlashAttention grid-size function. Verify: (N_h=32, S_q=2048, T_Q=64) -> 32*ceil(2048/64) = 32*32 = 1024; (N_h=16, S_q=1000, T_Q=128) -> 16*ceil(1000/128) = 16*8 = 128; (N_h=128, S_q=64, T_Q=64) -> 128*1 = 128. Assert exact equality.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes FlashAttention loop count L = ⌈S_kv / T_KV⌉ over the KV sequence length under macro-config T_KV.

verification.spec: Import the FlashAttention input-mapping function and call with several (N_h, S_q, S_kv) inputs and c_macro=(T_Q, T_KV). Assert returned L equals ceil(S_kv / T_KV) for all cases including non-divisible S_kv.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that treats grouped-query attention (GQA) as standard multi-head attention (MHA) when applying Φ, per the simplification in Section 4.2, so that attention Φ depends on query head count N_h rather than KV head count.

verification.spec: Call the FlashAttention Φ mapping with two inputs having identical (N_h_query, S_q, S_kv) but different kv_head counts (GQA settings). Assert Φ returns identical (G, L). Grep the implementation to confirm G is computed as N_h_query * ceil(S_q / T_Q), i.e., uses query head count and treats GQA as MHA.

sub_tasks.requirements: The FlashAttention configuration space is decomposed into C_macro = (T_Q, T_KV) and C_micro = (N_stg, N_wrp, ...) matching the vLLM Triton attention backend's tunable parameters.

verification.spec: Inspect the FlashAttention config enumeration. Assert C_macro=(T_Q, T_KV) and C_micro contains N_stg, N_wrp, and other vLLM Triton attention backend tunables. Cross-reference tunable names against the vLLM Triton attention backend's autotune configs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The joint configuration space C is expressed as the product C_macro × C_micro with a specific config c = (c_macro, c_micro), and macro/micro parameters are used consistently by downstream profiling, modeling, and runtime selection stages.

Code has been implemented that exposes, for each kernel, an enumeration of feasible C_macro and, given a fixed c_macro, an enumeration of feasible C_micro subject to hardware resource constraints (registers, shared memory) so that infeasible macro/micro combinations are excluded.

verification.spec: For each kernel, call enumerate_macro() and, for each c_macro, call enumerate_micro(c_macro). Verify: (a) enumerate_macro returns a non-empty list, (b) enumerate_micro(c_macro) may return a strict subset of the global C_micro when hardware constraints (shared memory, registers) rule out combinations, (c) launching the kernel with any pair in enumerate_macro x enumerate_micro(c_macro) does not raise CUDA out-of-resource errors on the target device.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that represents a full kernel configuration as a structured pair c = (c_macro, c_micro) and is consumed by the profiling, modeling, and runtime lookup stages via a shared schema.

verification.spec: Inspect the shared config schema (dataclass/pydantic model/dict spec) used across profiling, modeling, and runtime lookup. Assert it exposes both c_macro and c_micro as distinct sub-structures. Grep the three consumer sites (profiler, model-fit, runtime selector) and confirm they import this same schema rather than defining their own.

sub_tasks.requirements: The problem formulation c* = argmin_{c ∈ C} T(K, x, c) is realized as an executable optimization objective that consumes Φ(x) and the decomposed configuration space.

verification.spec: Import the optimizer module and verify it exposes a callable (e.g., select_config(kernel, x)) that (a) invokes the input mapping Phi to produce (G, L), (b) enumerates the decomposed C_macro x C_micro space, and (c) returns argmin over predicted latency. Inspect the source to confirm the objective form c* = argmin T(K, x, c) and that macro and micro spaces are iterated separately.

sub_tasks.requirements: Unit tests verify Φ correctness across kernels: for representative (M, N, K), (M_i, N, K, E), and (N_h, S_q, S_kv) inputs with chosen macro-configs, the computed (G, L) matches Table 2 formulas exactly, including the ceiling operations at boundary cases.

verification.spec: Run unit tests that call Phi for: (1) Dense GEMM with (M=1024,N=2048,K=4096) and (T_M=128,T_N=64,T_K=64), expect G=ceil(1024/128)*ceil(2048/64)=8*32=256, L=ceil(4096/64)=64; (2) Grouped GEMM with M_i=[100,200,300], N=2048, K=4096, E=3, macro (128,64,64), expect G=sum(ceil(M_i/128))*ceil(N/T_N); (3) FlashAttention with N_h=32, S_q=1024, S_kv=2048, (T_Q=64,T_KV=64), expect G=32*ceil(1024/64)=512, L=ceil(2048/64)=32. Include boundary cases where dims are not divisible by tile size to exercise ceiling.

sub_tasks.requirements: Sparse profiling over the (G, L) plane is implemented with wave-aligned partitioning, sub-interval sampling, aspect-ratio and head-alignment constraints, loop anchors, and per-config warmup/measurement iterations as described in Section 4.2.
The grid-size axis is partitioned into wave-aligned regions of width N_SM, each further split into I equal sub-intervals, exposing the ranges R_{w,i} = [a_{w,i}, b_{w,i}] used for sampling.
Code has been implemented to compute wave-aligned regions R_w = [(w-1)*N_SM + 1, w*N_SM] for w = 1..W, where N_SM is the number of SMs of the target GPU (e.g., 132 for H100, 148 for B200).

verification.spec: Call the wave-region computation function with N_SM=132 and W=3 and assert it returns [(1,132),(133,264),(265,396)]; repeat with N_SM=148 and W=2 and assert [(1,148),(149,296)].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to further split each wave region R_w into I contiguous sub-intervals R_{w,i} = [a_{w,i}, b_{w,i}] of (approximately) equal size, so that the union of sub-intervals equals R_w and adjacent sub-intervals do not overlap.

verification.spec: Call the sub-interval partition function with N_SM=132, W=2, I=4. Verify returned sub-intervals per wave partition [1,132] and [133,264] into 4 contiguous non-overlapping ranges of approximately equal size, and that union of sub-interval ranges equals the full wave range with no gaps or overlaps.

sub_tasks.requirements: Given (N_SM, W, I) the partitioning routine returns exactly W*I sub-intervals whose boundaries satisfy a_{w,1}=(w-1)*N_SM+1 and b_{w,I}=w*N_SM, and this is verified by a unit test.

verification.spec: Given N_SM=132, W=40, I=4, invoke the partitioning routine and assert it returns exactly 160 sub-intervals; assert first sub-interval starts at a_{1,1}=1 and last ends at b_{40,4}=40*132=5280.

sub_tasks.requirements: For GEMM-like kernels the sampled grid size g_{w,i} in each sub-interval is chosen as the largest value factorable into a 2D block grid <m_G, n_G> with m_G <= n_G and aspect-ratio rho(g_{w,i}) = n_G/m_G <= tau.

Code has been implemented that iterates candidate integers g in [a_{w,i}, b_{w,i}] from largest to smallest and returns the first g admitting a factorization g = m_G * n_G with m_G <= n_G and n_G/m_G <= tau.

verification.spec: Call the GEMM grid-selection routine with a sub-interval [100,132] and tau=1.1. Verify it iterates from 132 downward and returns the first g admitting factorization m_G*n_G with m_G<=n_G and n_G/m_G<=1.1 (e.g., 132=11*12 gives 12/11=1.09<=1.1, so returns 132). Verify it does NOT return g values whose only factorizations violate the aspect ratio.

sub_tasks.requirements: The aspect-ratio upper bound tau is exposed as a configurable parameter and its default value matches the paper (tau = 1.1) for Dense GEMM and Grouped GEMM profiling.

verification.spec: Inspect the profiling configuration module and assert that the tau parameter defaults to 1.1 for Dense GEMM and Grouped GEMM (e.g., via config.tau or function default argument). Confirm it is passed through to the grid-selection routine.

sub_tasks.requirements: For a representative sub-interval (e.g., R_{2,1} on an H100 with N_SM=132) the routine returns a grid size g and a factorization (m_G, n_G) satisfying both the interval-containment and aspect-ratio constraints, verified by a unit test.

verification.spec: For H100 (N_SM=132), W=2, I=4, take sub-interval R_{2,1} and call the selection routine. Assert the returned (g, m_G, n_G) satisfies a<=g<=b, g==m_G*n_G, m_G<=n_G, and n_G/m_G<=1.1.

sub_tasks.requirements: The selection routine never returns a factorization with n_G/m_G > tau, and this is exercised by a unit test that requests a sub-interval containing prime-only candidates to ensure fallback behavior is deterministic.

verification.spec: Call the selection routine with a sub-interval containing only primes (e.g., [11,13]) and tau=1.1. Since primes p have only 1*p factorization with ratio p, no g satisfies the constraint. Assert the routine either returns a deterministic sentinel (None) or a well-defined fallback, and never returns a factorization violating tau. Test is reproducible across multiple invocations.

sub_tasks.requirements: For attention kernels the grid dimension is aligned to the head-parallel launch structure by projecting the sub-interval upper bound to the nearest lower multiple of the head count N_h, subject to remaining within the sub-interval.
Code has been implemented that computes g_{w,i} = floor(b_{w,i} / N_h) * N_h and only accepts the result if g_{w,i} >= a_{w,i}, where N_h is the attention head count of the workload being profiled.

verification.spec: Call the attention grid-selection routine with sub-interval [100,132], N_h=32. Expect g = floor(132/32)*32 = 128, and 128>=100 so accepted. Test also [130,140] with N_h=64: floor(140/64)*64=128, but 128<130, so should return None or fallback.

sub_tasks.requirements: Given a head count N_h and a sub-interval [a,b] the routine returns a grid size divisible by N_h and contained in [a,b], verified by unit tests spanning N_h in {16, 32, 64, 128}.

verification.spec: Parametrize a unit test over N_h in {16,32,64,128} with sub-interval [200,400]. For each, assert the returned g satisfies (g % N_h == 0) and 200<=g<=400.

sub_tasks.requirements: A discrete set of loop anchors L is defined per kernel and combined with the sampled grid set G to form the profiling points (G, L) pairs.

For Dense GEMM and Grouped GEMM, the loop-anchor set corresponds to five K-dimension anchors spanning [1024, 5120] (e.g., {1024, 2048, 3072, 4096, 5120}), and is derived by dividing each K by T_K to obtain L values.

verification.spec: Inspect the profiling configuration for Dense/Grouped GEMM and assert the K-anchor list has exactly 5 entries spanning [1024,5120] (e.g., {1024,2048,3072,4096,5120}), and that loop anchors L are derived by dividing each K by T_K.

sub_tasks.requirements: For FlashAttention, KV sequence lengths are scaled by multipliers in [1.0, 3.0] to produce loop anchors that induce varying intra-block loop counts L, and the multiplier list is exposed as a configurable parameter.

verification.spec: Inspect the FlashAttention profiling config module and assert that KV-length multipliers are exposed as a configurable list, with default values contained in the interval [1.0, 3.0]. Verify multipliers are actually applied to derive KV lengths for loop-anchor generation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that produces the Cartesian product of the sampled grid set G and the loop-anchor set L as the set of structural profiling points, with |G| * |L| entries.

verification.spec: Given a sampled grid set G of size 10 and loop-anchor set L of size 5, invoke the profiling-point generator and assert the returned iterable has exactly 50 unique (G,L) pairs equal to the Cartesian product itertools.product(G,L).

sub_tasks.requirements: Sampled (G, L) pairs are translated into concrete executable kernel workloads following the unified abstraction (Section 4.2, workload instantiation equations).
For GEMM-like kernels, given macro-config <T_M, T_N, T_K> and factorization <m_G, n_G>, the profiling harness instantiates M = m_G * T_M, N = n_G * T_N, and K = L * T_K.

verification.spec: Invoke the GEMM workload instantiation function with macro=(T_M=128,T_N=64,T_K=64), (m_G,n_G)=(11,12), L=32. Assert returned (M,N,K) == (128*11, 64*12, 64*32) = (1408, 768, 2048).

sub_tasks.requirements: For attention kernels, given macro-config <T_Q, T_KV> and head count N_h, the profiling harness instantiates S_q = (G / N_h) * T_Q and S_kv = L * T_KV.

verification.spec: Invoke the attention workload instantiation function with macro=(T_Q=64,T_KV=64), G=512, N_h=32, L=32. Assert returned (S_q,S_kv) == ((512/32)*64, 32*64) = (1024, 2048).

sub_tasks.requirements: Grouped GEMM is reduced to the single-group (dense GEMM) case during structural profiling, and GQA attention is treated as multi-head attention, as stated in Section 4.2.

verification.spec: Inspect the profiling driver code and confirm: (1) Grouped GEMM profiling code path invokes the dense GEMM sampler with a single-group workload (E=1 or equivalent reduction), and (2) attention profiling code does not distinguish GQA-specific kv_head handling from MHA for the sampling step. Documented comments or dispatch branches should reflect this simplification.

sub_tasks.requirements: For each structural anchor <G, L, c_macro> every feasible c_micro in C_micro is evaluated via PyTorch Profiler with per-config warmup and measurement iterations.
The profiling loop performs exactly 3 warm-up iterations for each candidate micro-config before starting measurement, matching Section 4.2.

verification.spec: Instrument or mock the kernel-invocation call to count invocations before measurement starts. Run one profiling step for a single (G,L,c_macro,c_micro) and assert the counter equals exactly 3 warm-up calls prior to the measurement phase.

sub_tasks.requirements: The profiling loop performs exactly 5 measured iterations for each candidate micro-config and reports the average kernel latency T̄.

verification.spec: Instrument the kernel launch counter during the measurement phase and assert exactly 5 measured iterations occur; also verify the reported T̄ equals the arithmetic mean of the 5 measured latencies (compare against injected mock latencies).

sub_tasks.requirements: Kernel latency measurements are collected using torch.profiler.profile (PyTorch Profiler) as the unified data collection tool, and only the target kernel event's device time is recorded per iteration.

verification.spec: Inspect the measurement routine source and confirm it enters a `with torch.profiler.profile(...)` context around the measured kernel launches, and extracts device-time for the target kernel event only (e.g., filtering by kernel name). Confirm no alternative timer (cudaEvent, time.time) is used as the primary measurement.

sub_tasks.requirements: For each <G, L, c_macro>, the harness enumerates all micro-configs in C_micro that satisfy hardware feasibility constraints (e.g., shared memory and register limits) before profiling.

verification.spec: Call the micro-config enumeration function for a fixed (G,L,c_macro) and assert (a) the returned set is a subset of C_micro, and (b) all returned configs pass the feasibility check (shared memory usage <= device limit, registers/thread <= limit). Include a synthetic case where an infeasible c_micro (e.g., excessive stages causing SMEM overflow) is filtered out.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each profiling sample is recorded as the tuple <G, L, w, c_macro, c_micro, T̄>, where w = ceil(G / N_SM), and the resulting dataset is persisted for the modeling stage.

verification.spec: Run a minimal profiling sweep and load the persisted dataset (e.g., parquet/CSV/JSON). Assert every record contains fields (G, L, w, c_macro, c_micro, T_bar), and that w equals math.ceil(G/N_SM) for the target GPU's N_SM.

sub_tasks.requirements: Kernel-specific (W, I) profiling budgets are configured to match Section 5.1 for Dense GEMM, Grouped GEMM, and FlashAttention.
Dense GEMM and Grouped GEMM profiling uses W = 40 and I = 4, yielding 160 grid points per K-anchor, for each of five K anchors in [1024, 5120].

verification.spec: Inspect Dense/Grouped GEMM profiling configuration and assert W==40 and I==4. Assert the derived grid-point set per K-anchor has size 160 (=W*I), and that there are exactly 5 K-anchors within [1024,5120].

sub_tasks.requirements: FlashAttention profiling adapts W in [20, 35] based on query-head count q_head in [16, 128] (larger head counts get larger W) and uses I = 3, yielding 60–105 grid points per KV-length anchor.

verification.spec: For FlashAttention, call the W-selection function with q_head values {16,32,64,128}. Assert returned W is monotonically non-decreasing in q_head and lies in [20,35]. Assert I==3 across all cases. Verify the resulting per-anchor grid-point count = W*I lies in [60,105].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the total number of profiling samples as N_profile = |C_macro| * W * I * |L| * |C_micro| and logs this count before profiling starts.

verification.spec: Call the profiling driver with small mock sizes: |C_macro|=2, W=3, I=2, |L|=2, |C_micro|=4. Capture stdout/log and assert a line reports N_profile = 2*3*2*2*4 = 96 before profiling begins.

sub_tasks.requirements: The number of profiled configurations per <hardware, kernel> pair matches the values reported in Section 5.1.
Structural profiling for Dense GEMM produces approximately 74K configurations per <hardware, kernel> pair (within tolerance of the reported value).

verification.spec: Run WaveTune's sparse structural profiling pipeline for Dense GEMM on a single (hardware, kernel) pair (e.g., H100) with W=40, I=4, tau=1.1, and 5 K-dimension anchors in [1024, 5120].
